//: TNG-themed YoLink sensor history. Hand-authored fake data, expanded
into a doltlite raw store by `yolink-make-fixture` (see that binary's
docs for the generator). Obviously fictional: Enterprise-D compartments,
stardate-era timestamps.
start_ms is 2369-04-14T00:00:00+00:00 and interval_ms is 5 minutes, so
each device carries 288 samples ending exactly at the pipeline's pinned
Values are generated by a deterministic formula (see the binary), NOT a
random source: the fixture has to be byte-stable for Bazel to cache it.
They are meant to look plausible, not to be reproducible physics.

devices.name: ten_forward_cooler
devices.//: A drinks chiller behind the Ten Forward bar. Cycles either side of 3°C.

devices.name: stasis_unit_alpha
devices.//: Deep-freeze sample storage in the science labs; defrost cycle every ~4h.

devices.name: sickbay_plasma_fridge
//: DELIBERATELY REPORTS FAHRENHEIT. `temperature_f` is NOT reachable from
today's downloader — `download/mod.rs` pins each device kind to a fixed
CSV header and rejects a ℉ value under a ℃ header outright. The fixture
writes the metric straight into the raw store so the render side's
℉ → ℃ conversion (render/units.rs) is covered end to end, and so the
'two devices, two units, one axis' case has a real example. If a
downloader ever learns to emit ℉, this device stops being synthetic.
44.6°F is 7.0°C — the warmest of the three, so the converted series
is unmistakable on the shared axis.

devices.name: deck_12_water_main
//: Potable water feed for deck 12. `water_meter_gal` is a lifetime
totalizer (monotonic; `cumulative_of` names the per-sample metric it
sums) and `water_consumption_gal` is the volume drawn since the
previous sample. Both are gallons upstream and litres on the plot.
